title: 1-week TypeScript skill test plan
summary: Prepare for a timed TypeScript skill test: all 17 TypeScript lessons, the TypeScript flashcards, a practice run and the full timed simulator with two coding tasks. About 2 hours a day.

rhythm.text: Read three lessons, predict every snippet before you run it in the Playground, and note each gotcha you got wrong.
Finish the lessons, take a practice run, then sit the full timed test and review your weakest topics.

rules: Predict the output or the type before you run code or hover over it.
Work under strict mode: no any, no non-null assertions and no casts to silence an error.
Catch errors as unknown and narrow them before you read a property.
Prefer literal unions and as const objects; know what an enum compiles to before you use one.
Keep the timer honest in practice runs: no notes and no pausing.

typescript: Read a type error from the bottom up: the last line names the property that does not fit.
Narrow unions with typeof, in, instanceof or a discriminant before you use them.
Use satisfies to check a value against a type without widening it.
Reach for generics with constraints instead of any when a helper works on many types.
Add a never check in the default branch so a new union member breaks the build.

phases.title: Lessons, practice and the test
phases.check: Score 70% or more in every topic of the timed simulator, and pass both coding tasks within the time limit.

weeks.title: JavaScript runtime, the type system and the timed test
weeks.focus: Scope, this and equality, the event loop and promises, then types, variance, narrowing, generics, mapped and conditional types, enums, modules, classes and tsconfig. Finish with the full timed test.

tip.typescript: Turn on strict in every snippet you try, and check what the compiler infers before you add an annotation.
